newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * French President Jacques Chirac arrives for a two-day official visit to Romania on Friday, accompanied by Foreign Minister Herve de Charette, Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre and by Finance & Foreign Trade Minister Yves Galland, foreign ministry spokeswoman Gilda Lazar said.
French MPs and businessmen will also be part of Chirac's delegation, she said.
* Chirac will meet President Emil Constantinescu and Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea and speak to a session of parliament's two chambers.
* Debre and his Romanian counterpart Gavril Dejeu will sign a cooperation accord.

* Romania completed negotiations for integration into the Central European Free Trade Association (CEFTA), Lazar told a news conference. The accord making Romania a member will be signed in Bucharest in April by the trade ministers of the CEFTA countries and will be enforced starting July 1.
* Lazar said treaty talks between Romania and Ukraine will resume on February 26 in Kiev, with Romanian secretary of state Dumitru Ceausu attending.
* A delegation of U.S. Senate advisers arrives for a three-day visit on Friday to evaluate criteria for Romania's NATO membership.
* The draft budget could be presented to parliament in early March, Finance Minister Mircea Ciumara said.
He said all budget expenditure will be cut in 1997 due to large sums allocated for social security.
* The government will spend 10.04 percent of gross domestic product on social needs, an unprecedented proportion, Labour Minister Alexandru Athanasiu told a news conference.
He said the minimum monthly wage was set at 150,000 lei (less than $20).

* Romanian state television is on the verge of bankruptcy and its ratings are dropping dramatically, a U.S. expert told parliament's media standing commission. He said overstaffing and failure to allocate separate budgets for each department were the chief reasons for the crisis. State television, he said, was not able to compete with the private channels.
